01 / PROPOSAL LETTER

A connected platform for your dealer business

15 October 2026

To Md. Anowar Hossain Madina Natural Health Care Contact: 01730532966

Subject: Proposal for software development, implementation and support

Dear Mr. Hossain,

Tech Team IT Solution Ltd. is pleased to submit this proposal for a Dealer & Distribution Management System for Madina Natural Health Care, based on the revised feature requirements discussed with you.

The proposed solution connects the public website, dealer and sub-dealer network, field sales representatives (SR), product videos, orders, stock, dues, commissions, ranks, salary and withdrawals. Authorised staff will control daily operations, while dealers and sub-dealers access their permitted orders, earnings and network information.

The following pages describe the included modules, service arrangements and commercial terms. Fee, delivery and support fields are left blank for completion by the parties. Requested changes may be recorded on page 15 before signing. Product-specific discounts and commission rates are configurable.

Yours sincerely, For Tech Team IT Solution Ltd. Contact: 01333933667

03 / INCLUDED MODULES

Dealer & customer portal

A personal dashboard for approved users and dealers, with account information and records limited to their permitted access.

Ref.Module / featureIncluded scope
D01Profile & accountDisplay the approved profile. Users cannot edit their profile information; authorised administration staff can make corrections. Account login and password recovery are provided.
D02Product requestsSelect products and quantities, provide a payment transaction ID and submit an order / purchase request for administrative verification.
D03Order trackingView pending requests and subsequent order status. For unavailable stock, show the delivery estimate entered by administration. Once dispatched, show the courier name, tracking reference and supplied contact / slip details.
D04Stock & notificationsShow available and out-of-stock products. Display dashboard notifications when new products are added to stock, together with relevant order updates.
D05Dues & pending deliveryView unpaid purchase balances, later payments and adjustments. Separately view products or quantities still awaiting supply. Both panels display the same underlying history.
D06Wallet & withdrawalsView available earnings and submit a withdrawal request. Default minimum withdrawal: BDT 200, configurable by authorised administration. Display request and payment status.
D07Transaction historyView purchase, income, due adjustment, withdrawal and pending request records with dates, amounts and references.
D08Referral networkView a referral tree, downline counts and permitted purchase / transaction details. Provide a separate direct-referral list and a date-based transaction timeline.
D09Ranks & rewardsView achieved rank, qualification progress, incentives, bonuses and recorded rank increments under the configured business rules.

Referral access is restricted to the dealer's permitted network. Sensitive payment credentials and unrelated users' private records are not displayed in network reports.

Sub-dealer pricing, portal & salary

Sub-dealer purchase pricing - default example

Product MRPPurchase discountSub-dealer priceMargin at MRP resale
BDT 20040% = BDT 80BDT 120BDT 80 before expenses

This example uses a 40% discount. Each product can have a separate sub-dealer discount from 20% to 50%. The discount is reflected in the purchase price. Resale margin is realised through the sale of goods; separately earned wallet income follows the approved reward rules.

Flat monthly salary and tour allocation

BenefitRate and calculationExample
Sub-dealer salaryFlat 3% of the full monthly purchase amountBDT 50,000 × 3% = BDT 1,500
Sub-dealer tour allocation3% of the sub-dealer purchase valueBDT 120 × 3% = BDT 3.60

The flat 3% salary replaces the previous 1%, 2%, 3% and 4% monthly purchase tiers. Salary is accrued within the distribution schedule and paid through the monthly salary process, with each amount recorded once.

The 3% tour allocation is tracked separately from salary. Its use and release follow the approved tour policy. Authorised administration can change rates with an effective date.

Sales Representative (SR) panel

A controlled workspace for field sales staff, with accounts created by authorised administration and access limited to assigned duties and geographic areas.

Ref.Module / featureIncluded scope
SR01Admin-created accountsSuper Admin or explicitly authorised staff create SR accounts, assign the area / zone and activate, suspend or restore access. There is no public SR registration.

Access and handover checks

Demonstrate that an SR cannot self-register, see another area without permission, approve an order without authority, or access unrelated staff earnings. Demonstrate that withdrawing a permission also prevents the corresponding action.

SR salaries, targets and commission eligibility are configured under the approved company policy. Cash collection or payment approval access requires an explicit permission and recorded responsibility.

08 / BUSINESS RULES

Product pricing & configurable commissions

Each product has an MRP, cost / COGS and separate dealer and sub-dealer discount settings. Authorised administration can set each discount between 20% and 50%.

RuleIncluded behaviour
Purchase priceMRP × (1 - the applicable account-type discount). Show the applicable price before the request is submitted.
Default examplesAt MRP BDT 200: a dealer at 50% discount pays BDT 100; a sub-dealer at 40% discount pays BDT 120. These are examples, not fixed discounts for every product.
Distribution basisCommission percentages apply to the qualifying purchase value paid to the company. The default category schedules are shown on page 10.
Company retentionThe default worked examples reserve 30% of MRP for the company. Preview retained funds, allocations and any residual under the approved product policy.
Configurable rulesAuthorised staff may change category rates, approved dealer / user exceptions, recipients and eligibility with an effective date.
Historical recordsStore the applied price, discount and rule version for each approved order. Later changes apply to subsequent eligible approvals; past transactions and audit records remain intact.
Balanced allocationsValidate the company share and total allocations against the available purchase amount. Prevent an over-allocated configuration from being activated; show any unallocated balance for approved treatment.

Salary, tour and adjustments

The default sub-dealer salary is a flat 3% of the full qualifying monthly purchase amount; tour allocation is a separate 3%. Monthly settlement pays the recorded salary accrual once. Returns, cancellations and authorised corrections are recorded as linked adjustments under the approved policy.

The total distribution is a shared schedule across eligible recipients and funds. It is not a promise that a single purchaser receives every category. Discount, commission and salary rates can be revised prospectively by authorised administration.

09 / BUSINESS DISTRIBUTION

Dealer & sub-dealer commission distribution

This default example uses one product with MRP BDT 200 and dealer / sub-dealer discounts of 50% / 40%. Rates are configurable per the pricing policy on page 9. Distribution rates apply to the amount paid to the company: BDT 100 for a dealer or BDT 120 for a sub-dealer.

Pricing / available amountDealerSub-dealer
Purchase discount from MRP50% = BDT 10040% = BDT 80
Purchase value / distribution baseBDT 100BDT 120
Company share: 30% of MRPBDT 60BDT 60
Available for distributionBDT 40BDT 60
Distribution categoryDealer %Dealer BDTSub-dealer %Sub-dealer BDT
Referral commission10%10.0010%12.00
Area dealer commission10%10.0010%12.00
Own-dealer commission5%5.005%6.00
Dealer salary allocation2%2.002%2.40
Rank royalty4%4.004%4.80
Rank incentive2%2.002%2.40
Dealer-to-dealer (D2D)3%3.003%3.60
Marketing allocation2%2.002%2.40
Car / motorcycle incentive2%2.002%2.40
Additional rank reward--4%4.80
Sub-dealer salary--3%3.60
Sub-dealer tour allocation--3%3.60
TOTAL DISTRIBUTION40%40.0050%60.00

Area commission: management, division, district, upazila and union each receive a 2% allocation. D2D: first generation 2% plus second generation 1%.

The sub-dealer schedule retains the separate 4% rank reward and 4% rank royalty shown in the supplied flow. The 2% dealer salary allocation and 3% sub-dealer salary are separate categories. Beneficiaries follow the approved eligibility rules.

Dealer: BDT 100 = company BDT 60 + distribution BDT 40. Sub-dealer: BDT 120 = company BDT 60 + distribution BDT 60. The salary amounts above are accruals toward monthly salary, not an additional second salary payment.

11 / WORKFLOW & ACCEPTANCE

From product request to payment record

StepBusiness workflow
01 RequestDealer / sub-dealer selects products at the applicable price, enters the payment transaction ID and submits a request; an authorised SR may submit on the dealer's behalf. Both panels show the pending request.
02 VerifyAuthorised staff verify payment details, review available stock and approve, hold or reject the request with a recorded status.
03 FulfilStaff record stock issue and dispatch details. For unavailable or partially supplied items, the remaining quantity and expected supply date stay visible.
04 ReconcilePayments, credit dues and later adjustments update the shared order history and financial balance.
05 CalculateEligible earnings, referral rewards, rank progress and salary / incentive records follow the configured rules and approved recognition event.
06 WithdrawDealer requests a withdrawal; finance reviews it and records the payment result. The wallet, transaction history and reports reflect the same outcome.

15 / AGREEMENT TERMS

Ownership, confidentiality & changes

Source code and handover

After full payment of the agreed project fee, the customised system, database schema and related custom source code will be handed over to the client with ownership and full usage rights. Repository, deployment and credential transfer details are recorded on page 15. Third-party and open-source components remain subject to their respective licences.

Confidentiality and data security

Both parties will protect business strategy, cost information, dealer lists, commission rules, financial records, source code and security credentials during and after the engagement. Disclosure requires the other party's written consent, except where required by applicable law. The supplier may not sell or transfer the client's business data, dealer network or custom branding without written permission.

The supplier will provide appropriate access controls, secure credential handling and backup guidance. Hosting, backup frequency, retention, restoration responsibilities and support contacts will be recorded in the service schedule.

Changes, corrections and continuing support

Before signature, the client may add, remove or improve features using page 15. After signature, a new module, screen structure or workflow requires a written estimate and approval of its fee and time effect. Corrections required to meet the signed scope are included; after-delivery fault support follows the agreed support period. An optional monthly or annual maintenance agreement may be recorded separately.

External services and exclusions

Payment account setup and manual TrxID verification are included. Automated payment or courier API development must be expressly scheduled. Paid maps, SMS, gateway subscriptions, hosting and domain renewals are client costs unless marked included. Hardware, internet access, native Android / iOS apps, historical migration and bulk data entry require a written scope entry.

Termination and settlement

For a material breach, the affected party may give written notice allowing 15 working days to remedy it. If it remains unresolved, that party may terminate by written notice. The parties will reconcile payments against work completed and modules delivered, recording any balance, refund and handover due.

Applicable law and dispute resolution

The agreement is governed by the applicable laws of Bangladesh. The parties will first seek resolution through mutual discussion. If unresolved, they agree to refer the dispute to a mutually nominated arbitrator under the applicable arbitration law of Bangladesh.
